Hi Simon — thanks for the note and the timeline. Attaching a concise capability packet and the SCIM mapping template for your identity team. Also including a CSV admin-role matrix that enumerates our default roles (Org Admin, Tenant Admin, Support Operator, Auditor) plus custom role guidance.

Quick answers inline to the points you called out:
- SAML: we support HTTP-Redirect and HTTP-POST bindings, IdP-initiated flows, and metadata import. We do not require ADFS-specific patches; any ADFS that exposes standard metadata works. If you have encrypted assertions, we can accept them with a pre-shared cert.
- OIDC: we emit standard claims (sub, email, email_verified, groups) and optional claims for tenant_id and role_id. We can include custom claims on a per-tenant basis via the Console.
- SCIM: support for full replace and incremental (PATCH) operations per RFC 7644. We also offer a one-time bulk import tool for initial onboarding (CSV-to-batch SCIM import) and a continuous delta sync for user lifecycle updates.

Ben (cc'd) and Kimberly will add a short note on audit log retention and delegated admin scoping. We can join the Wed architecture sync — propose 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short demo of the SCIM provisioning flow.

Simon — quick technical addendum to Marissa's note:

1) RBAC and admin scoping
- Our RBAC model separates resource scoping (tenant vs. org) from privileges. Tenant Admin can create/delete models, manage routes, and configure tenant-level SSO. Org Admins manage billing, dedicated capacity assignments, and global policies. Support Operator role can view live requests, replay logs, and escalate but cannot access unredacted customer data. Auditor is read-only for audit logs and configuration.

2) Audit logs & retention
- Audit logs capture request metadata (timestamp, token id, route, model served, latency), admin actions (user created/role assigned), and config changes. Default retention is 12 months; we offer 3/5/7 year retention for enterprise contracts. Logs are exportable to your SIEM via S3 or syslog connector and delivered with HMAC-signed manifests for integrity verification.

3) SCIM specifics
- Delta syncs support incremental PATCH with startIndex and operations following canonical RFC semantics. The bulk import runs as a staged job with preflight validation; we provide a job-id and success/failure counts. For very large directories we recommend initial CSV import followed by an incremental connector.

If you want sample SAML metadata and an OIDC client configuration file for your IdP team, I can attach them.

—Ben

Evelyn — quick answers and links to artifacts:

- Encryption: Identity metadata and attribute values are encrypted at rest using tenant-scoped KMS keys by default for Dedicated and Private customers. Hosted customers get tenant-key encryption via our managed KMS with options for customer-managed keys (CMK). We can provide a KMS key rotation schedule and key policy excerpt.
- Tamper-evidence / HSM: Audit logs support HMAC signing out-of-the-box; for enterprise agreements we support HSM-backed signatures and split-key signing via a KMS/HSM integration. We can add an appendix with the HSM vendor integration notes.
- SCIM mapping: the attached scim_attribute_mapping_template.xlsx includes columns for externalId, employeeType, manager, costCenter, legalEntity and mapping examples. Our provisioning preserves custom attributes and passes them through to downstream entitlement layers.
- Test harnesses / runbook: we maintain a lightweight test harness repository that runs SAML metadata validation, assertion decoding, and OIDC claim inspection against a provided test IdP. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/SCIM-PLAYBOOK-GLTR (see section 'validation-harness'). Also attached is a one-page onboarding runbook enumerating steps, expected lead times (initial import 1–3 business days; SAML/OIDC verification 1 day; full SRP roll-out 2 weeks with staged validations).

Evelyn — brief note on delegated admin isolation:

We implement delegated admin scoping at both the API gateway and Console levels. Each admin session is tied to a scoped admin token that contains explicit allowed actions and resource filters. For Hosted customers we enforce least privilege by default; Dedicated/Private customers can define custom role templates and we support attribute-based access control (ABAC) predicates on tenant_id, directory_id, and environment tag.

Additionally, we provide a 'break glass' emergency access flow that requires multi-party approval (two internal approvers + time-bound temporary credentials) and is fully audited. Logs for emergency sessions are immutable and flagged for higher retention.

If you want, we can include sample API calls for role creation and an example JSON policy in a follow-up attachment.
